blocks.text: I can understand, ask and answer questions about my own and others’ future family plans in the future and conditional.
Tap the word to see what it means.

items.def: a form of verb used to express what would happen

blocks.text: The conditional expresses the idea of **would**. In French it is often followed by a second verb in the infinitive.

items: J’aimerais habiter en Suisse = I would like to live in Switzerland.
À sa place, je brulerais les lettres = In his/her place, I would burn the letters.

blocks.text: There is no separate French word for ‘would’. The spelling of the verb carries the meaning.
Regular -er verbs in the conditional use the **infinitive** as the stem. Add the imperfect tense endings: {-ais}, {-ais}, {-ait}. Tap a row to build the word.

blocks.q: The conditional of an -er verb is the infinitive plus the endings of which tense?
blocks.why: The conditional is formed by adding the imperfect tense endings to the infinitive stem, e.g. j’aimerais.

blocks.text: The conditional looks quite similar to the 1-verb future. Both have the same stem (the infinitive), but their **endings** are different.

blocks.q: Choose the correct form for the English meaning.

blocks.text: ‘Préférer’ (to prefer) and ‘tolérer’ (to tolerate) have two conditional spellings. The second spellings are newer and reflect better how these verbs are currently pronounced.
Where there is a choice, use the more modern spelling.
The verb ‘acheter’ is spelled with **è** in both the conditional (j’achèterais) and the 1-verb future (j’achèterai).

The stem is the infinitive, so the sound [r], as in ‘rue’, comes before the endings in both the conditional and the 1-verb future, e.g. mangerai, mangerais. The endings have [a] as in ‘animal’ and [ai] as in ‘vrai’.
-s and -t are silent at the end of a word. So all the singular conditional forms sound the same, and so do the tu and il, elle forms of the future.
Listen out for the pronouns: they tell you who is doing the action.
At the end of a verb, [ai] in the ‘je’ future form sounds like [é], like the [é] in ‘écrire’. This is an exception! Usually [ai] is pronounced as in ‘vrai’.

items.title: je commencerai
items.sub: I will start: sounds like the [é] in écrire

items.title: je commencerais
items.sub: I would start: sounds like the [ai] in vrai

blocks.text: The conditional endings all have the usual [ai] sound as in ‘vrai’, so you can hear the difference between je mangerais (I would eat) and je mangerai (I will eat).

blocks.q: Which one ends with the [é] sound?
blocks.why: The ‘je’ future ending -ai is pronounced [é]. The conditional ending -ais has the usual [ai] sound as in ‘vrai’.

blocks.q: Which one ends with the [ai] sound of ‘vrai’?
blocks.why: Conditional endings all have the usual [ai] sound. The ‘je’ future ending is the exception, pronounced [é].

slides.title: Saying what you would like to do

blocks.text: Use the conditional of ‘vouloir’ or ‘aimer’ + an infinitive to say what you would **like** to do. So ‘je voudrais’ and ‘j’aimerais’ both mean ‘I would like’.

items: Je voudrais jouer avec un frère ou une sœur = I would like to play with a brother or a sister.
Tu voudrais trouver un partenaire sympa = You would like to find a nice partner.
À l’avenir, il voudrait avoir deux enfants = In the future, he would like to have two children.

blocks.q: Match each question about starting a family to its meaning.

pairs.b: Are you going to start a family?
Would you like to start a family?

blocks.text: ‘Aimerais-tu fonder une famille ?’ also means ‘Would you like to start a family?’

blocks.q: Match the new words to their meanings.

blocks.label: When do you use ‘se séparer’?
blocks.text: Use ‘se séparer’ to talk about a couple breaking up.

items: The conditional is a verb form that expresses the idea ‘would’. It is often followed by a second verb in the infinitive.
The conditional of -er verbs is the infinitive stem + the imperfect endings, e.g. j’aimerais.
The sound [r] as in ‘rue’ is in all conditional and 1-verb future forms. The ‘je’ future ending -ai is pronounced [é].
Use the conditional of ‘vouloir’ or ‘aimer’ + an infinitive to say what you would like to do.

flashcards.back: The idea of ‘would’. It is often followed by a second verb in the infinitive.

flashcards.front: How do you form the conditional of a regular -er verb?
flashcards.back:
Infinitive stem + the imperfect tense endings.

j’aimerais

flashcards.front: Give the singular conditional forms of parler.
flashcards.back: je parlerais, tu parlerais, il/elle/on parlerait

flashcards.front: How can you tell the conditional from the 1-verb future when they have the same stem?
flashcards.back:
The endings are different.

future: je parlerai, tu parleras, il parlera
conditional: je parlerais, tu parlerais, il parlerait

flashcards.front: Say ‘I would like to live in Switzerland’ in French.
The verb ‘préférer’ has two conditional spellings. Which one should you use?
flashcards.back: The more modern one: je préfèrerais (rather than je préférerais).

flashcards.front: Which accent does ‘acheter’ have in the conditional and the 1-verb future?
Which sound comes before the endings in the conditional and the 1-verb future?
flashcards.back: [r], as in ‘rue’. The stem is the infinitive, so the [r] is in all their forms.

flashcards.front: Do the singular conditional forms sound different from each other?
flashcards.back: No. -s and -t are silent, so je mangerais, tu mangerais and il mangerait all sound the same.

flashcards.front: How is the ‘je’ ending of the 1-verb future pronounced?
flashcards.back: [é], like the [é] in ‘écrire’. It is an exception: je mangerai (I will eat) sounds different from je mangerais (I would eat).

flashcards.front: Which two verbs can you use in the conditional + an infinitive to say what you would like to do?
flashcards.back:
vouloir and aimer.

je voudrais / j’aimerais

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Tu aimerais ? Future and conditional with -er verbs (singular)
worksheet.instructions: Write your answers in French unless the question asks for English. Include the pronoun when the question shows one, and check your accents.

questions.prompt: Write in French, using the conditional of parler: ‘you (singular) would speak’.
questions.explanation: Infinitive parler + imperfect ending -ais = tu parlerais.

questions.prompt: Write in French, using the conditional of parler: ‘he would speak’.
questions.explanation: For il, elle, on the imperfect ending is -ait: parlerait.

questions.prompt: Write in French, using the 1-verb future of parler: ‘you (singular) will speak’.
questions.explanation: The 1-verb future of tu is the infinitive + -as: tu parleras.

questions.prompt: Write in French, using the conditional of aimer: ‘I would like’. Start with the short form of ‘je’ (j + apostrophe).
Fill the gap with the conditional of aimer: ______-tu fonder une famille ? (Would you like to start a family?)
questions.explanation: With tu, the conditional of aimer is aimerais.

questions.prompt: The conditional of -er verbs is the infinitive plus the endings of which tense? Answer with one word.
questions.explanation: The conditional endings are the same as the imperfect tense endings.

questions.prompt: ‘Préférer’ has two conditional spellings for je. Write the newer spelling, starting with je.
questions.explanation: The second spelling, préfèrerais, is newer and reflects how the verb is currently pronounced.

questions.prompt: Write in French, using the conditional of acheter: ‘you (singular) would buy’.
questions.explanation: ‘Acheter’ is spelled with è in the conditional: tu achèterais.

questions.prompt: Which of these ends with the [é] sound: ‘je mangerai’ or ‘je mangerais’? Write the one that does.
questions.explanation: The ‘je’ ending of the 1-verb future, -ai, is pronounced [é].
